spec.architecture:
1. Core compatibility model
GRACE 4 is a clean `.grace` model. New GRACE 4 skills and CLI commands do not validate, navigate, execute, or plan directly against GRACE 3 `docs/*.xml` artifacts. When a GRACE 3 project is detected, tooling may report guidance to use `grace-migrate`, but it must not enter dual-mode behavior.
2. Canonical `.grace` layout
.grace/ context/ requirements.xml technology.xml principles.xml deployment.xml ux-guidelines.xml
graph/ index.xml main.xml # optional segmented graph documents live here too
verification/ index.xml main.xml # optional segmented verification documents live here too
changes/ active/ C-CHANGE-ID/ spec.xml design-context.xml # optional curated rationale/context plan.xml
archive/ C-CHANGE-ID/ spec.xml design-context.xml # archived when present plan.xml
`context`, `graph`, and `verification` are durable current-state layers. `changes` is the temporal operational layer.
3. Standard artifact root tags
GRACE 4 standard XML artifacts use these root tags:
- GraceRequirements - GraceTechnology - GracePrinciples - GraceDeployment - GraceUXGuidelines - GraceGraphIndex - GraceGraphDocument - GraceVerificationIndex - GraceVerificationDocument - GraceChangeSpec - GraceChangePlan
The logical Current Graph is the projection of `graph/index.xml` plus graph documents. The logical Current Verification is the projection of `verification/index.xml` plus verification documents. They are not separate files.
4. Metadata and semantic anchors
Every GRACE 4 XML artifact root has mandatory `graceVersion="4.0"`.
Only root tags may carry artifact-level metadata attributes: - every root: `graceVersion`; - `GraceChangeSpec` and `GraceChangePlan`: `status`.
Semantic anchors are always XML tags and never attributes. This includes: - `GD-*` - `VD-*` - `C-*` - `M-*` - `V-M-*` - `DF-*` - `T-*`
Examples:
<GraceGraphDocument graceVersion="4.0"> <GD-AUTH> <M-AUTH-SESSION> ... </M-AUTH-SESSION> </GD-AUTH> </GraceGraphDocument>
<GraceChangeSpec graceVersion="4.0" status="approved"> <C-AUTH-SESSION-REFACTOR> ... </C-AUTH-SESSION-REFACTOR> </GraceChangeSpec>
`status` is an artifact lifecycle attribute for `GraceChangeSpec` and `GraceChangePlan`, not a semantic anchor. `C-*` remains a clean tag with no attributes.
5. Change status model
Allowed operational statuses: - draft - approved - applied - rejected - cancelled - superseded
Current-state invariants: - `.grace/changes/active/` may contain only `draft` or `approved` bundles; - `.grace/changes/archive/` may contain only `applied`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, or `superseded` bundles; - an executable bundle requires `spec.status = approved` and `plan.status = approved`; - an applied bundle requires both spec and plan to be `applied` and archived; - `superseded` bundles must reference a replacement `C-*`.
`grace-lint` validates current document state. Skills enforce transitions when operations occur.
6. Graph storage and routing
`graph/index.xml` routes graph anchors to graph documents:
<GraceGraphIndex graceVersion="4.0"> <GraphDocuments> <GD-MAIN> <Path>graph/main.xml</Path> <Owns> <M-AUTH-SESSION /> <DF-AUTH-TOKEN-FLOW /> </Owns> </GD-MAIN> </GraphDocuments> </GraceGraphIndex>
The owning document must contain the matching wrapper tag and the actual definitions:
<GraceGraphDocument graceVersion="4.0"> <GD-MAIN> <M-AUTH-SESSION> ... </M-AUTH-SESSION>
<DF-AUTH-TOKEN-FLOW> ... </DF-AUTH-TOKEN-FLOW> </GD-MAIN> </GraceGraphDocument>
Graph invariants: - every `GD-*` in the graph index maps to exactly one path; - every graph document contains exactly one matching `GD-*` wrapper; - every `M-*` and `DF-*` listed in the index exists exactly once inside the owning `GD-*`; - every `M-*` and `DF-*` found in graph documents is listed in the index; - cross-document links are allowed but must reference existing anchors; - physical segmentation is reversible: monolithic and segmented layouts with the same content produce the same logical projection.
7. Verification storage and routing
`verification/index.xml` routes verification anchors to verification documents:
<GraceVerificationIndex graceVersion="4.0"> <VerificationDocuments> <VD-MAIN> <Path>verification/main.xml</Path> <Owns> <V-M-AUTH-SESSION /> </Owns> </VD-MAIN> </VerificationDocuments> </GraceVerificationIndex>
The owning document contains the matching wrapper and aggregate verification contracts:
<GraceVerificationDocument graceVersion="4.0"> <VD-MAIN> <V-M-AUTH-SESSION> ... </V-M-AUTH-SESSION> </VD-MAIN> </GraceVerificationDocument>
Verification invariants: - every `VD-*` in the verification index maps to exactly one path; - every verification document contains exactly one matching `VD-*` wrapper; - every `V-M-*` listed in the index exists exactly once inside the owning `VD-*`; - every `V-M-*` found in verification documents is listed in the index; - every `M-*` in the graph projection has exactly one corresponding `V-M-*`; - the correspondence is deterministic: `V-` + `M-*`; - each `V-M-*` is an aggregate verification contract and may contain multiple scenarios, commands, log markers, trace assertions, and gates.
8. Project context semantics
All five context artifacts are mandatory. `requirements`, `technology`, and `principles` are always applicable. `deployment` and `ux-guidelines` may be explicitly marked `not-applicable`, but only with a real reason; "not a web app" is not sufficient.
Context meanings: - `requirements.xml`: what the project must accomplish, user/business/product requirements, acceptance constraints, and scope; - `technology.xml`: runtime, languages, package managers, frameworks, tooling, compatibility targets, and technical constraints; - `principles.xml`: project-specific engineering principles, methodology rules, architecture preferences, safety rules, and agent behavior constraints; - `deployment.xml`: delivery, publishing, runtime, installation, release, hosting, distribution, and documentation-delivery surfaces; - `ux-guidelines.xml`: user/developer/operator/agent interaction guidelines, including visual UI when relevant, CLI UX, API ergonomics, docs examples, error messages, approval flows, and terminology.
9. Change bundle artifacts
Each change bundle lives under `.grace/changes/active/C-*/` until it is closed and archived. It may contain: - `spec.xml` with `GraceChangeSpec` (normative intent/source of requirements); - optional `design-context.xml` (explanatory curated rationale, alternatives, assumptions, deferred decisions, scenarios; non-normative); - `plan.xml` with `GraceChangePlan` (normative execution plan).
`GraceChangeSpec` stays concise and intent-focused. `design-context.xml` preserves rationale without expanding requirements. `GraceChangePlan` contains the executable contract: intent summary, assertions, scopes, tasks, dependencies, and per-task acceptance criteria.
10. Baseline/target assertions
`GraceChangePlan` must contain machine-checkable `BaselineAssertions` and `TargetAssertions` using a limited core vocabulary: - `MustExist` - `MustNotExist` - `MustOwn` - `MustLink` - `MustVerify` - `MustPassCommand` - `MustContain` - `MustNotContain`
Assertions are validation contracts, not a mutation DSL. Agents apply changes through normal read/edit workflows; CLI validates the resulting state.
11. Scope and conflict model
`GraceChangePlan` must contain: - `DurableScope`: planned writes to `.grace` durable truth, such as graph anchors, verification anchors, context artifacts, and optionally whole `GD-*`/`VD-*` documents for split/merge/rehome operations; - `ObservedWriteScope`: planned writes outside durable `.grace`, such as source files, tests, package manifests, README/release docs, generated files, and packaged mirrors.
No mandatory `ObservedReadScope` exists in core. Read context belongs in task packets and planning context, not in the artifact model.
Multiple approved active plans may overlap in `DurableScope` and may coexist. Overlap at planning/approval time is a strong warning, not a hard block. Overlap blocks only unsafe concurrent/parallel execution. Sequential execution is allowed after fresh preflight. If another change made the plan stale, `BaselineAssertions` fail and the plan must be superseded/replanned through normal flow.
12. Execution idempotency and recovery
GRACE 4 does not introduce a mandatory persistent execution/run artifact. `grace-execute` must be idempotent and recovery-aware by inspecting: - active/archived change artifacts; - current durable `.grace` state; - observed filesystem/code state; - git/worktree state when available; - assertions and validation diagnostics.
On rerun against an active approved change, `grace-execute` performs recovery preflight and derives one of these states: - clean-to-start; - partial-observed-writes; - durable-state-changed; - target-already-satisfied; - unsafe-unknown-drift.
Safe states may continue/retry after explicit user confirmation. Unknown drift, failed baseline, or ambiguous partial writes hard-stop and require rollback, superseding change, or reconciliation through normal GRACE workflows. `grace-execute` must never silently mark a change applied and must never silently rewrite an approved plan.

component.name: Artifact Grammar
component.responsibility: Defines the GRACE 4 XML grammar: standard root tags, mandatory `graceVersion`, allowed operational `status` attribute, semantic-anchor tag rules, required sections, current-state invariants, assertion vocabulary, scope structure, ownership consistency, and extension policy. It is custom grammar enforced over parsed XML, not XSD and not regex parsing.

component.name: XML Parser Adapter
component.responsibility: Wraps `fast-xml-parser` to parse GRACE artifacts consistently, preserve dynamic tag names, preserve CDATA boundaries, report parse errors with file locations where possible, and provide normalized nodes to Artifact Grammar validators.

component.name: Project Context Store
component.responsibility: Owns mandatory context artifacts under `.grace/context`: requirements, technology, principles, deployment, and ux-guidelines. It validates applicability semantics and provides stable domain, stack, delivery, interaction, and agent-behavior context to skills.

component.name: Current Graph
component.responsibility: Stores accepted durable graph truth through `GraceGraphIndex` and `GraceGraphDocument` artifacts. Routes `M-*` and `DF-*` anchors through `GD-*` ownership entries and preserves explicit cross-document semantic connectivity.

component.name: Current Verification
component.responsibility: Stores accepted durable verification truth through `GraceVerificationIndex` and `GraceVerificationDocument` artifacts. Routes aggregate `V-M-*` verification contracts through `VD-*` ownership entries and maintains deterministic `M-*` to `V-M-*` coverage.

component.name: Graph Logical Projection
component.responsibility: Builds a deterministic unified current graph view from monolithic or segmented graph storage. Validates duplicate anchors, missing index routes, ownership mismatch, dangling links, and lossless segmentation/merge equivalence.

component.name: Verification Logical Projection
component.responsibility: Builds a deterministic unified current verification view from monolithic or segmented verification storage. Validates duplicate `V-M-*`, missing routes, ownership mismatch, module-to-verification coverage, and lossless segmentation/merge equivalence.

component.name: ChangeSpec Artifact
component.responsibility: Defines `GraceChangeSpec`: concise normative change intent, user-visible outcome, scope expectations, non-goals, constraints, acceptance direction, and exactly one `C-*` semantic anchor. It is created as draft by `grace-spec` and may become approved, rejected, cancelled, applied, or superseded according to lifecycle rules.

component.name: Change Design Context Artifact
component.responsibility: Defines optional `design-context.xml` inside a change bundle. It stores curated non-normative rationale, rejected alternatives, assumptions, deferred decisions, scenarios, and external constraints. It is read by `grace-plan` as context only; `spec.xml` wins on conflict.

component.name: ChangePlan Artifact
component.responsibility: Defines `GraceChangePlan`: intent summary, BaselineAssertions, TargetAssertions, DurableScope, ObservedWriteScope, implementation tasks with `T-*` anchors, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and verification gates. Approved plans are immutable; replacement requires a new `C-*` bundle.
component.depends-on: Artifact Grammar, ChangeSpec Artifact, Assertion Evaluator, Scope and Conflict Detector

component.name: Assertion Evaluator
component.responsibility: Evaluates the core assertion vocabulary for baseline preflight and target validation: `MustExist`, `MustNotExist`, `MustOwn`, `MustLink`, `MustVerify`, `MustPassCommand`, `MustContain`, and `MustNotContain`.
component.depends-on: Graph Logical Projection, Verification Logical Projection, Project filesystem

component.name: Scope and Conflict Detector
component.responsibility: Reads DurableScope and ObservedWriteScope across active changes, surfaces overlap as derived operational state, warns during planning/approval, and blocks only unsafe concurrent or parallel execution. It does not prevent overlapping approved plans from coexisting.

component.name: grace-init Skill / CLI Support
component.responsibility: Creates a complete `.grace` skeleton for a new GRACE 4 project: context artifacts, graph index/document, verification index/document, and empty change active/archive directories. It does not create dummy change bundles and does not overwrite existing artifacts without confirmation.

component.name: grace-spec Skill
component.responsibility: Interviews the user, creates a `C-*` change bundle with draft `GraceChangeSpec`, creates/updates optional change design context when warranted, presents the spec for approval, and transitions the spec to approved/rejected/cancelled through explicit user choice.
component.depends-on: ChangeSpec Artifact, Change Design Context Artifact, Project Context Store

component.name: grace-plan Skill
component.responsibility: Reads approved `GraceChangeSpec` plus optional design context and current durable state, then creates draft `GraceChangePlan` with assertions, scopes, tasks, and verification gates. It surfaces scope overlaps as strong warnings, refuses spec-plan mismatch, and requires explicit user approval before `status="approved"`.
component.depends-on: ChangeSpec Artifact, ChangePlan Artifact, Current Graph, Current Verification, Assertion Evaluator, Scope and Conflict Detector

component.name: grace-execute Skill
component.responsibility: Executes active approved change bundles. It performs preflight, recommends sequential or parallel-safe mode, waits for explicit user choice, applies observed changes, verifies, centrally updates durable `.grace` state, validates targets, marks spec/plan applied, and archives the bundle. It is idempotent and recovery-aware without a mandatory persistent run artifact.
component.depends-on: ChangePlan Artifact, Assertion Evaluator, Scope and Conflict Detector, grace-lint

component.name: grace-migrate Skill
component.responsibility: Provides the only GRACE 3 to GRACE 4 bridge. It reads legacy GRACE 3 artifacts, produces a migration draft/report, asks for explicit approval, agent-applies `.grace` artifacts, validates the result, and deletes legacy docs only after successful validation plus explicit confirmation. It does not create retroactive `C-*` bundles.
component.depends-on: Artifact Grammar, grace-lint, Project Context Store, Current Graph, Current Verification

component.name: grace-refresh Skill
component.responsibility: Detects drift between durable `.grace` current state and observed repository state. It does not silently mutate durable state; it helps create reconciliation changes through the normal `GraceChangeSpec`/`GraceChangePlan` lifecycle.
component.depends-on: Current Graph, Current Verification, ChangeSpec Artifact, ChangePlan Artifact

component.name: grace-status Skill / CLI Command
component.responsibility: Reports durable health, validation summaries, active/archive change activity, derived overlap/block states, stale plans, explained change contexts, and unexplained observed drift. It reports current document state and derived states without modifying XML statuses.
component.depends-on: grace-lint, Scope and Conflict Detector, Graph Logical Projection, Verification Logical Projection

component.name: grace-lint Validator
component.responsibility: Authoritative current-state validation for `.grace`: artifact grammar, version consistency, root attributes, semantic-anchor discipline, graph/verification ownership, projections, assertions, lifecycle location invariants, package-specific release checks, and autonomy readiness where applicable.
component.depends-on: XML Parser Adapter, Artifact Grammar, Graph Logical Projection, Verification Logical Projection

component.name: CLI Navigation Commands
component.responsibility: Rewrite `grace module`, `grace verification`, and `grace file` to resolve `.grace` graph/verification/file-local anchors. They are navigation/reporting commands only and must not implement dual-mode v3 behavior.
component.depends-on: Graph Logical Projection, Verification Logical Projection, Artifact Grammar

component.name: GRACE 4 Skill Surface
component.responsibility: Publishes GRACE 4 skills: `grace-init`, `grace-spec`, `grace-plan`, `grace-execute`, `grace-refresh`, `grace-status`, `grace-ask`, `grace-fix`, `grace-refactor`, `grace-verification`, `grace-reviewer`, `grace-cli`, `grace-explainer`, `grace-migrate`, and `grace-setup-subagents`. `grace-multiagent-execute` is removed from the published GRACE 4 surface.

component.name: Marketplace Packaging Surface
component.responsibility: Keeps canonical skills, packaged mirrors, marketplace/plugin manifests, package metadata, openpackage metadata, README, release notes, and validation scripts synchronized for the GRACE 4 release.

testing.strategy: Build deterministic tests around parsed XML fixtures, Artifact Grammar validation, logical projection construction, lifecycle state validation, assertion evaluation, execution recovery classification, migration safety, and marketplace packaging integrity. Tests should prefer fixture projects that model complete `.grace` states and invalid variants. GRACE 4 release validation must include Bun tests, CLI validation, and marketplace/package drift checks.

non-goals.non-goal: No dual-mode GRACE 3/GRACE 4 support in core skills or CLI. GRACE 4 works only with `.grace`.

Do not migrate this repository's own operational GRACE 3 `docs/` artifacts as part of this spec. The repository remains operationally GRACE 3 until GRACE 4 exists and can migrate through `grace-migrate`.
No CLI-applied migration. Migration is agent-applied through the `grace-migrate` skill; CLI validates and reports only.
No executable graph delta DSL. Assertions are validation contracts, not mutation operations.

No mandatory persistent execution/run artifact. `grace-execute` must be idempotent and recovery-aware through current state, scopes, assertions, observed files, git/worktree state when available, and validation.
No published `grace-multiagent-execute` in GRACE 4. Parallel-safe execution is a mode of `grace-execute`.
No XSD as the source of truth for Artifact Grammar. Use `fast-xml-parser` plus custom grammar validation.
No adoption profiles or GRACE-lite mode in core. GRACE 4 core is Full GRACE.
No automatic destructive cleanup during migration. Legacy docs deletion requires valid `.grace` and explicit confirmation.
No hard global segmentation thresholds. Segmentation is planner-owned; tooling may provide warnings and heuristics.
